doc.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013

title: Rock and roll class and his concerts and critics' workshops
summary: He teaches the lost highways of migration and describes the 1976-79 concerts at Buffalo State with workshops that brought in critics such as Crouch, Giddins and Gitler.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: my rock & roll class we do the lost highways. You know, here’s what these guys were traveling. Then you had the white guys, Merle Haggard and these guys who went out to California, you know, first picking grapes and then potatoes, and then you had the black guys who were going to their various places, first Chicago and then later California. And then you have Charles Brown and Nat Cole. He could play piano. And they had those independent record companies. Oh my God. What a world. And I get to teach about it. And when I did my — all my concerts that I did, I did this with a couple of students when Elvis Costello, Buffalo State Loves Jazz, all these things. Steve [s/l] Rebufsky. And we were doing this stuff in ’76, ’77, ’78, ’79. And I always made sure we did workshops, you know, and that we brought in the critics. We brought in Stanley Crouch — I just got his new book, you know, Kansas City Lightning, the study of Charlie Parker and Kansas City. Gary Giddins. Ira Gitler. Don DeMichael. I brought them all in. 1978. And then I did 1979, we did another thing and I brought other critics in. Ben Sidran and the Heath Brothers. And I made sure I brought in Jackie & Roy and, I forget who the other one was, the electric guitar player, his wife wrote a book about him, one of the first fusion players, oh I can’t think of his name right now. And then I started doing these other projects you know. And I always made sure the education was there. Who were writing the books and who had the magazines. Galen Garth. He got all of those old Cash Box magazines and he got the rights to them, so I have all those things that he left for me, it was really nice. Terrific.
